question: Refer to the exhibit. Which feature must be implemented on Postman to receive the response from a Cisco Nexus 9000 Series Switch?
context: Postman GUI: GET request to http://10.10.10.70/api/mo/sys/intf/phys-[eth1/3].json. Authorization tab, TYPE dropdown showing options: Inherit auth from parent, No Auth, API Key, Bearer Token, Basic Auth, Digest Auth, OAuth 1.0, OAuth 2.0, Hawk Authentication, AWS Signature, NTLM Authentication [Beta]. Body tab shows a JSON response with interface attributes (adminSt enable, autoNeg, bw, delay, dot1qEtherType, etc.).
options: username and password in the Nexus-cookie
username and password in the api/mo header
certificate in the HTML, Nexus-API header
theory: After authenticating (POST to aaaLogin), an APIC REST session is tracked by a session token carried in a cookie named APIC-cookie; to make a subsequent GET succeed in Postman, that API token must be attached in the APIC-cookie, not sent as plain username/password in a header or presented as a certificate — matching the token/cookie-based session model the book describes for aaaLogin. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 16 — Automation and Scripting Tools)
